answer: Each identity must bind a one-time iris scan: the scanner hashes the iris into a crystal-clear template and stores only the hash, never the image. One human yields exactly one template, so a sybil farmer needs a thousand real eyeballs for a thousand puppets, a cost no script can forge. Ferrous gates and cameras make the check physical, not a hollow form: liveness detection rejects photos and printed irises. Limits: scanners are scarce in some regions, a leaked registry exposes templates, and a determined attacker could still pay strangers to scan.
